topic: Prompt caching for chatbots: put the static prefix first so repeat input tokens cost a fraction (Anthropic docs)
text:
Your chatbot re-sends the same system prompt and tool list on every single message. You're paying full price for it each time.

Anthropic's prompt caching docs: a cache read costs 0.1x the base input price for most models, a 5-minute cache write costs 1.25x, and the cache refreshes for free each time it's used.

What decides whether you get hits:
• The cached prefix is built in this order: tools, then system, then messages
• Put stable content first, per-user or changing content last
• A hit needs a 100% identical prefix, so one changed tool description invalidates tools, system and messages
• Default lifetime is 5 minutes; a 1-hour TTL costs 2x to write

My rule of thumb: never put a timestamp or user name at the top of the system prompt. It silently breaks every hit.

If you run a chatbot, do you log cache read vs cache write tokens per request?

image.alt: Four cards on Anthropic prompt caching: cache reads cost 0.1x, prefix order tools system messages, identical prefix required, 5-minute default lifetime, signed Ali Hassan, alihexan.com
